sections.h2: Which Mahoning County offices handle a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Three offices share the work. The County Auditor values every parcel and keeps the tax list, the County Treasurer collects the money, and the Board of Revision hears value complaints. The auditor's office is at 120 Market Street in Youngstown and answers at 330-740-2010. The treasurer sits on the first floor of the same courthouse and takes calls at 330-740-2460, Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

The county's own consumer leaflet says the auditor cannot raise or lower taxes. Rates come from the budget requests of schools, townships, cities and the county, approved by voters and computed under Ohio Department of Taxation procedures. If a Mahoning County owner dislikes the rate, the leaflet points to budget hearings and the taxing bodies themselves, not to the auditor.

sections.h2: What does Mahoning County look like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Mahoning County covers 425 square miles on Ohio's eastern edge, next to Pennsylvania. It was carved out of Trumbull and Columbiana counties and formed on March 1, 1846, with Youngstown as the seat and largest city. The 2020 census counted 228,614 residents, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 224,706, so the county has been shrinking since its peak around 1970.

Twenty public school districts serve the county, from Youngstown City and Boardman Local to Canfield, Poland, Austintown, Struthers and Western Reserve. Which district a house sits in changes both the tax rate and the buyer pool, so check the district printed on the bill.

Census QuickFacts shows a market on the affordable end for Ohio:

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home, 2020 to 2024: $154,700
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 70.3 percent
  • Median gross rent: $791
  • Households: 98,065, averaging 2.25 people
  • Residents 65 or older: 24.4 percent

That last figure matters for taxes, because senior relief programs reach a large share of Mahoning owners.

sections.h2: How does the auditor set value, and what caps the increase?
sections.html:
Ohio taxes 35 percent of market value, and the county's leaflet says all real property must be revalued every six years, with a new inspection of exteriors in each cycle. Market value means the price a willing seller would take from a willing buyer. Appraisers study sales and apply them to the property record, so a wrong bedroom count or a missing garage can raise a value without the owner noticing.

Two limits soften increases. House Bill 920, passed in 1976, gives a credit on voted millage so that a reappraisal does not bring in more money from existing levies. More recently, the treasurer's site explains that House Bill 186 created an Inflation Cap Credit for qualifying property classes. The state had to make a one-time mid-cycle change to rates, which delayed bills statewide, and the treasurer says an overpayment from the change comes back as a credit or refund.

Timing also trips up sellers. The auditor's FAQ says taxes run a year behind and a parcel is taxed by its condition on January 1. A building torn down in the spring can still show on the next bill, and a split or combination recorded in one year takes effect on the following year's tax list.

sections.h2: When and how are Mahoning County taxes paid?
sections.html:
Bills come in two halves, and the treasurer posts the due date on its home page each cycle. The second-half deadline for 2026 was September 18, 2026, later than usual because House Bill 186 delayed the bills. The page warns that missing a bill does not cancel the 10 percent penalty for late payment, so a seller who has not received one should ask the treasurer for a copy.

Ways to pay, as listed by the Mahoning County Treasurer
MethodWhat the treasurer's page says
OnlineCards, e-check, Apple Pay, Google Pay and Samsung Pay. Cards carry 2.5 percent with a $2.00 minimum, e-check carries $1.50
Phone(330) 408-6150, any hour. Payments post the next business day
In personCourthouse first floor, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Friday
MailCheck or money order to 120 Market Street, Youngstown, OH 44503. No cash. Postmark on or before the due date counts

The treasurer also cautions that a postmark now often shows the day the post office machine handled the envelope, which can be days after drop-off. Pay electronically, mail early, or ask the post office counter for a hand-stamped postmark.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Mahoning County property value?
sections.html:
File a Complaint Against the Valuation of Real Property with the Board of Revision. Its three statutory members are the County Auditor, the County Treasurer and the president of the county commissioners, and a quorum of two decides each case. The complaint window opens in January and closes March 31. The deadline for tax year 2025 was March 31, 2026, and filing for tax year 2026 begins in early January 2027.

The Board is clear that a hearing covers value, not tax rates or the pain of a larger bill. The owner carries the burden of proof. Evidence the auditor's page suggests for a house includes:

  • A sale within the last 24 months, with the settlement statement and a notarized arm's-length affidavit
  • A tax-purpose appraisal from a certified appraiser
  • Photographs paired with professional repair estimates
  • Builder-certified costs for construction five years old or less

Neighborhood disputes, pets nearby, sewer trouble and the fact that you changed nothing on the property do not count as value evidence. Mail the form to the Board of Revision at the auditor's office, 120 Market Street, Youngstown, or hand it in. The Board is not responsible for lost mail, so follow up until you hold a date-stamped copy.

sections.h2: What tax relief can Mahoning County owners apply for?
sections.html:
Ohio gives a non-business credit automatically on residential and farm parcels, and an owner-occupancy credit that must be applied for if the owner is not already receiving it. Beyond those, the auditor lists:

  • Homestead Exemption. For owners who live in the home, with an income cap, and who are 65, permanently disabled, or a qualifying surviving spouse. The cap for tax year 2025 was $40,000 and rises to $41,000 for tax year 2026. For 2025 the protected value was $29,000, or $58,000 under the enhanced version for disabled veterans and surviving spouses of public service officers, which has no income test.
  • CAUV farm valuation. Land of 10 acres or more used only for commercial agriculture, or smaller land earning an average of $2,500 a year. Applications are filed after the first Monday in January and before the first Monday in March, and the auditor must receive them by then.
  • Recoupment. Leaving CAUV charges three years of the tax savings, which a farm seller should ask the auditor about before closing.

The auditor's page also says the state updates CAUV soil values every three years, with the next change applying to tax year 2026.

sections.h2: What should a Mahoning County seller check on the tax account before closing?
sections.html:
Start with the balance. The treasurer's office, reached at 330-740-2460, handles delinquent taxes, so ask it what is owed on the parcel before a buyer signs. Special assessments from outside bodies, such as lighting or lawn-cutting charges, appear in the tax breakdown. Mortgages, mechanic's claims and judgments do not appear on the bill. For those, ask the County Recorder at 330-740-2345 and the Clerk of Courts at 330-740-2104.

Next, line up the deed. Acreage and parts of platted lots go to the GIS and Tax Map table at 21 West Boardman Street for review before the auditor will transfer them. Deeds also need the marital status of the seller, a tax mailing address, a legal description and a prior deed reference, as the auditor's checklist spells out. The same checklist prints the county's conveyance fee as $1.00 per $1,000, a permissive fee of $3.00 per $1,000 and a transfer fee of 50 cents per parcel; ask the auditor to confirm the total for your sale price.

Whatever the condition of the house, unpaid tax lines will surface on the title search. Settle them with the treasurer before the closing date.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Mahoning County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the County Treasurer at 330-740-2460 about payments and balances, and the County Auditor at 330-740-2010 about value, exemptions and forms. Both offices are in the courthouse complex at 120 Market Street, Youngstown.

faqs.q: What is the last day to file a Board of Revision complaint?
faqs.a: March 31 of the year after the tax year in question. The window for tax year 2025 closed on March 31, 2026, and filing for tax year 2026 opens in early January 2027.

faqs.q: Does a new roof or an unfinished repair list lower my valuation?
faqs.a: It can, if you document it. The Board accepts photographs paired with professional repair estimates, but the owner has to prove the value is too high. A general complaint about higher taxes will not succeed.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Mahoning County property tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes, online or by phone. The treasurer's page lists a 2.5 percent card fee with a $2.00 minimum and a $1.50 charge for e-check, both collected by the payment vendor, not the county.

faqs.q: Will I owe farm recoupment if I sell land enrolled in CAUV?
faqs.a: Possibly. The auditor says that leaving the program, or failing to qualify, brings a charge equal to three years of taxes. If a buyer files a new application or the prior owner has renewed on time, acreage can stay enrolled, so ask the auditor before the sale.
